newsitem.title: USA: Burlington Resources, LL&E to merge.
newsitem.headline: Burlington Resources, LL&E to merge.

text.p: Burlington Resources Inc and Louisiana Land and Exploration Co said Thursday they have signed an agreement to merge in a deal valued at $3 billion.
Under terms of the agreement, LL&E would merge with a subsidiary of Burlington in an exchange of stock.
LL&E shareholders would receive shares of Burlington based on a fixed exchange ratio of 1.525 Burlington shares for each LL&E share held.
The companies said they expect the deal to be accounted for as a pooling of interests and to qualify as a tax-free reorganization.
They expect the deal would be accretive to cash flow per share in 1997 and beyond. The combination would result in a 75 percent-25 percent mix between natural gas and oil production.
The merged company would have long-term debt comprising 40 percent of the book capitalization of the company, and current cash and short-term investments totaling about $500 million.

Upon completion of the deal, Burlington president and chief executive Bobby Shackouls would be chairman, president and CEO of the combined company, which would be known as Burlington Resources and would be headquartered in Houston.
H. Leighton Steward, chairman, president and CEO of LL&E, would be vice chairman and chairman of the executive committee of the board.

Under terms of the agreement, LL&E will merge with a subsidiary of Burlington in an exchange of stock in which LL&E shareholders will receive shares of Burlington based on a fixed exchange ratio of 1.525 Burlington shares for each LL&E share held.

Based on Burlington's closing price of $46.125 on Wednesday, July 16, the 35.9 million LL&E shares on a fully diluted basis, and the assumption by Burlington of about $500 million of LL&E debt, the deal has a total value of about $3 billion.
The companies expect the deal would be completed in about three months.

Current combined worldwide natural gas production is 1.7 billion cubic feet per day, liquids production is about 90,000 barrels per day, operating cash flow is about $1 billion per year and equity market capitalization is about $8.2 billion.
